value: Sanchez, D.L., Johnson, N., McCoy, S.T., Turner, P.A. and Mach, K.J. (2018). Near-term deployment of carbon capture and sequestration from biorefineries in the United States. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115(19), 4875-4880. doi:10.1073/pnas.1719695115

Locator: printed page numbers (4875-4880). The main paper does NOT print capex, compression power or an energy figure for the capture-compression step: it prints supply-curve costs only. The Supporting Information (SI Text, with the capture and compression cost method from McCollum and Ogden 2006 and the per-plant parameters) is not held; capex and kWh/t CO2 cannot be extracted until it is obtained. Loaded: the fermentation CO2 factor, the typical cost per t CO2 (reprinted from other works), the project financial parameters, and the model supply-curve results in other-values (under 25 US$/tCO2 for 60% of CO2; under 32 for 90%). The cost-per-gallon equivalence is 0.05 US$/gal. The emission factor is cited as ref. 19 (Hornafius and Hornafius 2015). Price year of the capture cost not stated: publication year 2018 used. Not loaded: transport and sequestration costs (pipeline is a separate archetype but a per-ton-km cost with an ambiguous ton is in other-values), policy credits and profits.
Supporting Information not held (Fig. S1, S2 and SI Text referenced). The main text prints "pipeline costs ... dollars per ton-kilometer" without saying short or metric ton.
